title: Atomic compatibility tuple v1
description: The unit everything in the product means when it says "exact certified tuple". docs/integrations/UNIVERSAL_AGENT_COMPATIBILITY.md is the normative owner and packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql#source_certifications is the persistence owner. The tuple is atomic: change any one dimension and it is a different tuple with its own certification, because a certification of one agent on one operating system through one observation mode says nothing about any other combination. Its digest is SHA-256 over the RFC 8949 core deterministic CBOR encoding of this record with tuple_digest omitted, computed the way D-261 computes every planning policy digest, so two implementations cannot disagree about the identity of a tuple. D-058 makes trust digest-addressed: an artifact is named by its digest and never by a mutable version string alone.

observation_mode.description: Exactly the nine modes packages/schemas/observer-equivalence-v1.json declares, in that spelling, because a second vocabulary for one concept is the duplication SR-009 exists to remove. The mode is part of the tuple because two modes observing one execution have different precedence and different evidence ceilings, which is what D-098 records for adapter one: the metrics channel supersedes the session log and the two are never summed.

platform_profile_id.description: A profile_id in packages/schemas/platform-profile-registry-v1.json. The platform is part of the tuple because the key-protection class, the supervision mechanism and the isolation strength all differ between profiles, and the evidence ceiling depends on them.

duplicate_domain.description: The exclusivity unit this tuple observes within, from packages/schemas/observer-equivalence-v1.json. Two tuples sharing a duplicate domain compete for one execution and exactly one counts.

artifact.description: The collector or adapter binary that does the observing, named by digest under D-058. A mutable name or version never establishes official identity on its own.

source.description: The agent product being observed, and the exact version range the certification covers. A range rather than a single version because a patch release usually does not move the observation surface; an open-ended range is refused, because an unbounded upper bound is a certification of software that does not exist yet.

schema_url.description: The producer's declared telemetry schema, where it has one. Null is a fact rather than an omission: adapter one's measured producer emits neither a schema URL nor a semantic-conventions version, and D-264 records that.

accounting.description: Which arithmetic turns this source's numbers into Token Burn, bound by identity and digest so a profile edit changes the tuple rather than silently changing what a certified tuple means.

privacy_binding.description: What the tuple is allowed to observe and what it must remove before anything is queued. This is part of the tuple rather than a property of the adapter because a certification is a statement about a privacy boundary as much as about an arithmetic: D-099 makes the adapter-one strip a collector obligation performed at the device boundary, and a tuple whose strip list changed is a different tuple.

rejects_undecodable_datapoint.description: Whether a datapoint from which a forbidden attribute cannot be removed is rejected whole. False is not certifiable: D-099 admits no partial strip.
